title: 100. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Density as Mass per Unit Volume
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Density as Mass per Unit Volume
questions.learningObjective: Calculate density from given mass and volume.
questions.question: A block has a mass of \(120\text{ g}\) and a volume of \(40\text{ cm}^3\). What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume. Here, \(120 \div 40 = 3\), so the density is \(3\text{ g/cm}^3\). The choice "\(30\text{ g/cm}^3\)" would result from dividing \(120\) by \(4\) instead of \(40\).

questions.learningObjective: Identify a correct unit for density.
questions.question: Which of the following is a unit of density?
questions.explanation: Density is mass per unit volume. A mass unit divided by a volume unit gives a density unit, such as \(\text{g/cm}^3\). The unit \(\text{g/cm}\) is a mass per length, which is not density.
questions.hint: Recall that density compares mass with volume.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate mass when density and volume are known.
questions.question: A liquid has a density of \(2\text{ g/cm}^3\). What is the mass of \(5\text{ cm}^3\) of this liquid?
questions.explanation: Mass is density multiplied by volume. Here, \(2 \times 5 = 10\), so the mass is \(10\text{ g}\). The choice "\(2.5\text{ g}\)" would result from dividing \(5\) by \(2\), which is not the correct relationship.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate volume when density and mass are known.
questions.question: A metal sample has a mass of \(300\text{ g}\) and a density of \(1.5\text{ g/cm}^3\). What is its volume?
questions.explanation: Volume is mass divided by density. Here, \(300 \div 1.5 = 200\), so the volume is \(200\text{ cm}^3\). The choice "\(450\text{ cm}^3\)" is the product \(300 \times 1.5\), which is not the volume.

questions.learningObjective: Determine which of two objects has the greater density.
questions.question: Object P has a mass of \(60\text{ g}\) and a volume of \(20\text{ cm}^3\). Object Q has a mass of \(80\text{ g}\) and a volume of \(40\text{ cm}^3\). Which object has the greater density?
questions.explanation: Density of Object P is \(60 \div 20 = 3\text{ g/cm}^3\). Density of Object Q is \(80 \div 40 = 2\text{ g/cm}^3\). Since \(3 > 2\), Object P has the greater density.
questions.hint: Calculate the density of each object separately before comparing.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate density in \(\text{g/cm}^3\) after converting mass from kilograms to grams.
questions.question: A substance has a mass of \(0.5\text{ kg}\) and a volume of \(250\text{ cm}^3\). What is its density in \(\text{g/cm}^3\)?
questions.explanation: Convert \(0.5\text{ kg}\) to grams: \(0.5 \times 1000 = 500\text{ g}\). Then density is \(500 \div 250 = 2\text{ g/cm}^3\). The choice "\(0.002\text{ g/cm}^3\)" would result from dividing \(0.5\) by \(250\) without converting units.
questions.hint: Convert the mass to grams before dividing by volume.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate mass from density and volume in a liquid context.
questions.question: A liquid has a density of \(0.8\text{ g/cm}^3\). What is the mass of \(500\text{ cm}^3\) of this liquid?
questions.explanation: Mass is density multiplied by volume. Here, \(0.8 \times 500 = 400\), so the mass is \(400\text{ g}\). The choice "\(625\text{ g}\)" would result from dividing \(500\) by \(0.8\), which is not the correct relationship.
questions.hint: Multiply the density by the volume to find the mass.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate density in \(\text{kg/m}^3\) from given mass and volume.
questions.question: A solid has a mass of \(2.4\text{ kg}\) and a volume of \(0.003\text{ m}^3\). What is its density in \(\text{kg/m}^3\)?
questions.explanation: Density is mass divided by volume. Here, \(2.4 \div 0.003 = 800\), so the density is \(800\text{ kg/m}^3\). The choice "\(0.0072\text{ kg/m}^3\)" is the product \(2.4 \times 0.003\), which is not the density.
questions.hint: Divide the mass in kilograms by the volume in cubic metres.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate density after finding volume from the dimensions of a block.
questions.question: A metal block has a mass of \(1.35\text{ kg}\) and dimensions \(10\text{ cm}\) by \(5\text{ cm}\) by \(3\text{ cm}\). What is its density in \(\text{g/cm}^3\)?
questions.explanation: The volume of the block is \(10 \times 5 \times 3 = 150\text{ cm}^3\). Convert the mass to grams: \(1.35 \times 1000 = 1350\text{ g}\). Then density is \(1350 \div 150 = 9\text{ g/cm}^3\). The choice "\(0.9\text{ g/cm}^3\)" would result from dividing \(135\) by \(150\).
questions.hint: Find the volume from the dimensions, convert mass to grams, then divide mass by volume.

questions.concept: Volume from Density and Mass with Unit Conversion
questions.learningObjective: Calculate volume in \(\text{cm}^3\) after converting mass from kilograms to grams.
questions.question: A substance has a density of \(2.5\text{ g/cm}^3\). What volume is occupied by \(0.5\text{ kg}\) of this substance?
questions.explanation: Convert \(0.5\text{ kg}\) to grams: \(0.5 \times 1000 = 500\text{ g}\). Volume is mass divided by density: \(500 \div 2.5 = 200\), so the volume is \(200\text{ cm}^3\). The choice "\(1250\text{ cm}^3\)" is the product \(500 \times 2.5\), which is not the volume.
questions.hint: Convert the mass to grams first, then use \(\text{volume} = \text{mass} \div \text{density}\).
